project.name: ModelPlanning
project.description: Research codebase for studying planning in GPT-style language models: it generates context-free grammar, path-finding, and OpenWebText datasets, trains models with next-token or multi-token prediction losses, trains VQ-VAEs on hidden representations, and estimates mutual information between representations and future tokens.

nodes.name: NLP_mi_calc_v6 2.py
nodes.summary: Distributed script that computes mutual information between per-block VQVAE3v2 codes and last-token VQVAE codes extracted from a GPT model's hidden states on OpenWebText-style NLP data, streaming counts into StreamingInfo.
nodes.languageNotes: Filename contains a space ('v6 2'), suggesting a duplicated copy of a script version; it cannot be imported as a Python module.

nodes.name: load_state_dict_remove_ddp_prefix
nodes.summary: Loads a checkpoint state dict into a model after stripping DDP 'module.' and torch.compile '_orig_mod.' prefixes, with diagnostic reporting of mismatched keys.

nodes.name: build_vqvae3v2_from_config
nodes.summary: Constructs an Encoder3v2/Decoder3v2/VQVAE3v2 stack from a saved config dictionary for block-level hidden-state quantization.

nodes.name: compute_vq3v2_index
nodes.summary: Encodes hidden states through a VQVAE3v2 and returns the discrete codebook index for a single sample.

nodes.name: compute_vq3v2_index_batch
nodes.summary: Batched version of VQVAE3v2 code index computation over hidden-state tensors.

nodes.name: get_batch
nodes.summary: Samples a random batch of token windows from a memory-mapped binary dataset split and moves it to the device.

nodes.name: save_streaming_info_counts
nodes.summary: Serializes StreamingInfo count tables and metadata to disk for later MI analysis.

nodes.name: collect_block_mi
nodes.summary: Computes mutual information values between each block's code variable and the last-token code from a StreamingInfo instance.

nodes.name: load_vqvae_last_token_model
nodes.summary: Loads a VQVAELastToken model from a checkpoint folder, rebuilding it from saved config and stripping DDP prefixes.

nodes.name: sync_and_update_streaming_info
nodes.summary: Gathers code samples from all distributed ranks and updates StreamingInfo counters on the master process.

nodes.name: calculate_and_report_metrics
nodes.summary: Computes current entropy and MI estimates from StreamingInfo and logs them.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses arguments, sets up DDP, loads the GPT and VQVAE models, iterates over data batches extracting hidden states and codes, and streams MI statistics with periodic checkpointing.

nodes.name: information_theory_utils.py
nodes.summary: Provides StreamingInfo, a stream-friendly count-table container for estimating entropy, joint/conditional entropy, mutual information and conditional MI over discrete variables, with plug-in and Paninski/BUB bias-corrected estimators and optional HDF5 sample storage.
nodes.languageNotes: Optional dependency pattern: h5py/numpy/scipy imported in a try/except with feature flags (HDF5_AVAILABLE, SCIPY_AVAILABLE).

nodes.name: StreamingInfo
nodes.summary: Maintains Counter-based count tables for chosen variable combinations as samples stream in, exposing entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and Paninski/BUB/BAG bias-corrected estimators, plus optional HDF5 sample flushing and reloading.

nodes.name: test_independent_uniform
nodes.summary: Sanity test checking that MI between independent uniform variables is near zero and entropies match log of alphabet size.

nodes.name: test_copy_variable
nodes.summary: Sanity test checking that MI between a variable and its copy equals its entropy.

nodes.name: test_three_variables
nodes.summary: Sanity test for joint, conditional entropy and conditional MI across three related variables.

nodes.name: test_no_samples
nodes.summary: Checks that querying StreamingInfo with no samples raises or handles the empty case correctly.

nodes.name: mi_calc_full_path.py
nodes.summary: Top-level script that runs a trained GPT on path-finding prompts, encodes hidden states with two-stage VQVAE1/VQVAE2 and a Path_VQVAE, and estimates mutual information between the resulting discrete codes across the full generated path.
nodes.languageNotes: Written as a flat module-level script with wildcard imports (from minimal_VQVAEs import *), so most logic runs at import time rather than in functions.

nodes.name: sync_and_update_streaming_info
nodes.summary: Gathers sampled code tuples from all DDP ranks and feeds them into the per-pair StreamingInfo trackers on the master process.

nodes.name: calculate_and_report_metrics
nodes.summary: Computes current entropy and mutual information estimates from the StreamingInfo trackers and logs them.

nodes.name: create_plots_and_save
nodes.summary: Generates matplotlib plots of mutual information results (e.g. MI vs. time offset / code pairs) and saves figures plus raw results to the output directory.

nodes.name: minimal_VQVAEs.py
nodes.summary: Large model library defining many VQ-VAE variants (single, two-stage, layer/block, last-token, path, 3v2, 61) with transformer-based encoders/decoders, codebook usage tracking, cosine push and soft-entropy regularizers, and input normalization, used to quantize LLM hidden states.
nodes.languageNotes: Many classes duplicate the same method set (normalize_codebook_vectors, compute_cosine_push_loss, update_usage_tracking, ...) instead of sharing a base class.

nodes.name: ResidualBlock
nodes.summary: Residual MLP block (output = x + MLP(x)) with optional LayerNorm used inside VQVAE encoders/decoders.

nodes.name: CustomSequential
nodes.summary: Thin nn.Sequential subclass that forwards extra arguments through its transformer blocks.

nodes.name: VQVAE_single
nodes.summary: Implements a single-stage VQ-VAE over flattened hidden states, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking, input normalization and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: VQVAE1
nodes.summary: Implements the first-stage VQ-VAE that quantizes per-layer hidden states via Encoder1/Decoder1, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking, per-layer normalization and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: Encoder1
nodes.summary: Layerwise transformer encoder that processes each layer's hidden state with its own TransformerBlock stack and aggregates across layers.

nodes.name: Decoder1
nodes.summary: Transformer decoder that expands an aggregate latent back into per-layer hidden-state reconstructions.

nodes.name: Encoder3
nodes.summary: Layerwise-plus-aggregate transformer encoder for the VQVAE3 model.

nodes.name: Decoder3
nodes.summary: Aggregate-then-layerwise transformer decoder for the VQVAE3 model.

nodes.name: VQVAE3
nodes.summary: Implements the VQVAE3 model built from Encoder3/Decoder3, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking, normalization and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: VQVAE2
nodes.summary: Implements the second-stage VQ-VAE that quantizes sequences of first-stage codes/latents via Encoder2/Decoder2, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: Encoder2
nodes.summary: Transformer encoder for second-stage VQVAE2 over temporal sequences of first-stage latents.

nodes.name: Decoder2
nodes.summary: Transformer decoder reconstructing first-stage latent sequences for VQVAE2.

nodes.name: VQVAELastToken
nodes.summary: VQ-VAE specialised for the last-token hidden state, with configurable MLP encoder/decoder builders, activation selection, cosine push loss and usage tracking.

nodes.name: VQVAE3_Modified
nodes.summary: Subclass of VQVAE3 overriding the cosine push loss with log-scaling and count-division variants.

nodes.name: Path_Encoder
nodes.summary: Simple encoder for path-level VQ-VAE inputs.

nodes.name: Path_Decoder
nodes.summary: Simple decoder for path-level VQ-VAE reconstructions.

nodes.name: Path_VQVAE
nodes.summary: Implements a VQ-VAE over path-finding sequence representations, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: Encoder3v2
nodes.summary: Revised encoder for VQVAE3v2 operating on transformer block hidden states.

nodes.name: Decoder3v2
nodes.summary: Revised decoder for VQVAE3v2 reconstructing block hidden states.

nodes.name: VQVAE3v2
nodes.summary: Implements the VQVAE3v2 block-level model, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking, normalization and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: Encoder_layer
nodes.summary: Encoder for the layer-wise VQVAE_layer model.

nodes.name: Decoder_layer
nodes.summary: Decoder for the layer-wise VQVAE_layer model.

nodes.name: VQVAE_layer
nodes.summary: Implements a VQ-VAE over a single transformer layer's hidden states, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: Encoder61
nodes.summary: Encoder for the VQVAE61 model used in path-finding experiments.

nodes.name: Decoder61
nodes.summary: Decoder for the VQVAE61 model used in path-finding experiments.

nodes.name: VQVAE61
nodes.summary: Implements the VQVAE61 model for path-finding hidden states, including codebook normalization, cosine push and soft-entropy losses, codebook usage tracking, stochastic masking and a forward pass returning reconstruction, quantization indices and losses.

nodes.name: modules.py
nodes.summary: Core transformer building blocks (LayerNorm, rotary positional embeddings, rotary self-attention with flash attention support, MLP, TransformerBlock) used by the VQ-VAE encoders/decoders, plus self-tests.

nodes.name: LayerNorm
nodes.summary: LayerNorm with optional bias.

nodes.name: RotaryPositionalEmbedding
nodes.summary: Computes rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) and applies rotate-half rotation to query/key tensors.

nodes.name: RotarySelfAttention
nodes.summary: Multi-head self-attention with rotary embeddings, optional causal/padding masks and PyTorch flash attention fallback.

nodes.name: MLP
nodes.summary: Feed-forward GELU MLP sub-layer of a transformer block.

nodes.name: TransformerBlock
nodes.summary: Pre-norm transformer block composing LayerNorm, RotarySelfAttention and MLP with residual connections.

nodes.name: test_attention_combinations
nodes.summary: Tests RotarySelfAttention outputs across causal and padding-mask combinations.

nodes.name: test_rotary_norm_preservation
nodes.summary: Verifies rotary embeddings preserve vector norms.

nodes.name: test_gpu_flash
nodes.summary: Compares flash-attention and manual attention outputs on GPU.

nodes.name: NLP_llm_train.py
nodes.summary: Script-style training loop for a GPT model on memmapped OpenWebText token bins, supporting DDP, mixed precision, gradient accumulation, cosine LR schedule and checkpointing.
nodes.languageNotes: nanoGPT-style module-level training script: configuration via globals, DDP setup through torchrun environment variables.

nodes.name: get_batch
nodes.summary: Samples random contiguous windows from train/val uint16 memmap token files and returns pinned input/target tensors shifted by one token.

nodes.name: estimate_loss
nodes.summary: Evaluates mean loss over eval_iters batches for both train and val splits with the model in eval mode.

nodes.name: NLP_vqvae_layer_and_block_train.py
nodes.summary: Trains VQVAE3v2 models on hidden states of a frozen pretrained NLP GPT, either per layer or per block of layers, with cosine LR, masked NRMSE reconstruction metrics and codebook-usage logging/plots.

nodes.name: get_batch
nodes.summary: Samples random max_attention_window-length token windows from the memmapped train/val bins for feeding the frozen GPT.

nodes.name: get_lr
nodes.summary: Cosine learning-rate schedule with linear warmup for the VQ-VAE optimizer.

nodes.name: process_hidden_states_for_vqvae3v2_layer

nodes.name: process_hidden_states_for_vqvae3v2_block
nodes.summary: Groups consecutive layers (delta_b per block) of GPT hidden states into stacked block tensors with norm-based normalization for block-level VQVAE3v2 training.

nodes.name: llm_train.py
nodes.summary: Main training script for GPT models on context-free-grammar sequences with next-token or multi-token (MTL) targets, DDP support, periodic CFG accuracy evaluation and metadata/checkpoint saving.

nodes.name: get_batch
nodes.summary: Samples memmapped CFG token windows and builds either a single shifted target or a list of multi-token-ahead targets for MTL training.

nodes.name: estimate_loss
nodes.summary: Estimates average train/val loss over eval_iters batches with gradients disabled.

nodes.name: llm_train_utils.py
nodes.summary: Shared training helpers: cosine LR schedule with warmup, human-readable training metadata export, parallel CFG validity evaluation of model completions, accuracy logging and CFG loading from dataset pickles.

nodes.name: get_lr
nodes.summary: Returns learning rate for an iteration using linear warmup followed by cosine decay to min_lr.

nodes.name: save_training_metadata
nodes.summary: Writes model architecture, training parameters and system config to JSON and readable text files in the output directory.

nodes.name: evaluate_cfg_accuracy

nodes.name: load_cfg_from_dataset

nodes.name: model.py
nodes.summary: GPT transformer implementation with rotary positional embeddings, optional attention masks, multi-token-prediction (mtl) heads/losses, generation with EOS handling, and hidden-state extraction APIs used by VQ-VAE and MI scripts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a @dataclass GPTConfig and PyTorch nn.Module subclasses; falls back to manual attention when flash attention (scaled_dot_product_attention) is unavailable.

nodes.name: rotate_every_two
nodes.summary: Rotates adjacent value pairs (x0,x1)->(-x1,x0) along the last dim for rotary embeddings.

nodes.name: apply_rotary_pos_emb
nodes.summary: Applies precomputed rotary cos/sin embeddings to query/key tensors.

nodes.name: LayerNorm
nodes.summary: LayerNorm variant with optional bias.

nodes.name: CausalSelfAttention
nodes.summary: Multi-head causal self-attention with rotary embeddings, merged causal/padding masks and flash-attention fallback.

nodes.name: MLP
nodes.summary: Transformer feed-forward block: linear, GELU, projection and dropout.

nodes.name: Block
nodes.summary: Pre-norm transformer block combining attention and MLP with residual connections.

nodes.name: GPTConfig
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding GPT hyperparameters such as block size, vocab size, layers, heads, embedding dim and dropout.

nodes.name: GPT
nodes.summary: Full GPT language model with weight-tied embeddings, NTP/MTL loss computation, optimizer configuration, MFU estimation, autoregressive generation and hidden-state extraction.

nodes.name: path_finding_llm_train.py

nodes.name: get_batch
nodes.summary: Pulls the next batch from persistent train/val DataLoader iterators (resetting epochs via samplers) and builds single or multi-token shifted targets.

nodes.name: estimate_loss
nodes.summary: Estimates average train/val loss over random batches with gradients disabled.

nodes.name: estimate_loss_consistent
nodes.summary: Computes validation loss over a fixed, deterministic set of validation batches so loss is comparable across iterations.

nodes.name: evaluate_accuracies
nodes.summary: Runs path-finding accuracy evaluation on the model, records it in an accuracy history and prints results.

nodes.summary: Normalizes first-stage VQVAE1 outputs using precomputed per-dimension statistics.

nodes.name: 22188_Internal_Planning_in_Lan.md
nodes.summary: Markdown conversion of the ICLR 2026 paper 'Internal Planning in Language Models: Characterizing Horizon and Branch Awareness' (Ustaomeroglu, Askin, Joshi, Joe-Wong, Qu; CMU). It introduces the VQ-VAE + mutual-information pipeline this codebase implements and reports planning-horizon, branch-awareness and computational-history results on CFG, path-finding and OpenWebText.

nodes.name: VQ-VAE + MI Pipeline
nodes.summary: The paper's core method (§2, Fig. 1): for a frozen LM, (1) train a VQ-VAE that maps a collection of hidden-state blocks G_S to a discrete code Z_S, (2) encode the dataset and count co-occurrences of code pairs (Z_A, Z_B), (3) estimate I(Z_A; Z_B) and normalized MI from those counts. Every experiment in this repo follows these three stages.

nodes.name: Hidden-State Compression (VQ-VAE Codes)
nodes.summary: Hidden activations h_t^l are redundant and high-dimensional, so the paper compresses variable-sized blocks of them with a transformer encoder/decoder VQ-VAE and a nearest-neighbour codebook (straight-through gradients). The resulting codes are coarse summaries of internal computation, not semantic units.

nodes.name: Codebook Regularizers (L_cos, L_ent)
nodes.summary: Beyond reconstruction and the standard VQ/commitment loss, the paper adds a cosine-similarity penalty pushing codebook vectors apart and an entropy term discouraging code collapse (Eq. 3, App. A.1-A.2), so codes are both compact and discriminative. Implemented as cosine-push and soft-entropy losses.

nodes.name: Count-Based MI and nMI
nodes.summary: MI between discrete codes is estimated from empirical joint/marginal counts; normalized MI (nMI) divides by the maximum MI within the same analysis, so only relative within-setting comparisons are claimed. App. E analyses finite-sample error and a bias-corrected estimator.

nodes.name: NTP vs. MTP Training
nodes.summary: Models are trained either with next-token prediction (NTP) or multi-token prediction (MTP, following Gloeckle et al. 2024: shared trunk, separate heads per future token). Inference is always standard autoregressive decoding. Finding: MTP only weakly modulates planning; no consistent NTP/MTP difference overall.

nodes.name: Architecture-Matched GPT Models
nodes.summary: The LMs under study are GPT-3 Small style decoder-only transformers with rotary position embeddings (an 8-layer model for OpenWebText; a 0.3B scale-up in App. D.1). After training they are frozen and their per-block outputs are treated as the fundamental units of computation.

nodes.name: Horizon of the Plan (§3.1)
nodes.summary: Measures nMI between the code of all prefix activations (layers 1..L-1) and the last-layer decision-state code of each generated token x_{T+tau}. CFG: nMI decays fast (short, local plan). PF: nMI stays high and can peak at later intermediate nodes, consistent with working backwards from the goal. Planning horizon is task-dependent.

nodes.name: Branches in the Plan (§3.2)
nodes.summary: On PF samples with two correct paths and one disjoint decoy path, compares I(Z_prefix; Z_alt) / I(Z_prefix; Z_decoy), where path codes come from a separate path VQ-VAE. Ratios above 1 (7.6 NTP / 6.3 MTP on PF-Short; 1.45 / 1.82 on PF-Long) show the prefix keeps information about unused correct branches.

nodes.name: Information in the Computational History (§3.3)
nodes.summary: Diagnostic on OpenWebText: per-layer prefix hidden states are split into 16-token blocks B_k^l and compared with the decision-state code via nMI and conditional nMI. Last layers and most recent blocks carry the most information (recency effect), yet earlier layers/blocks stay measurably informative.

nodes.name: Context-Free Grammar Task
nodes.summary: Synthetic CFG (Allen-Zhu, 2024) whose tokens carry intrinsic meaning and are governed by local and global syntactic rules; a controllable stand-in for natural language. Sentences of length 16-67 with prefixes of length 8-24 (App. B.2.1).

nodes.name: Path-Finding Task (PF-Short / PF-Long)
nodes.summary: Graphs over 28 node tokens are linearised as shuffled edge lists; the model must output a path from fixed start node 1 to goal node 2. PF-Short needs paths of length 4, PF-Long length 6. Each sample has two correct paths and a disjoint decoy (App. B.2.2).

nodes.name: OpenWebText Natural Language
nodes.summary: Real-world natural text (Gokaslan et al., 2019) used for the computational-history diagnostic, tokenised with GPT-2 BPE (App. B.2.3).

nodes.name: Probing vs. MI (Confound Argument)
nodes.summary: The paper motivates MI over learned codes by arguing that probe accuracy conflates probe capacity with what the representation encodes and can violate data-processing; App. D.2-D.3 show probe-based quantities tracking nuisance factors. No probing code is included in this repository.

layers.description: The ICLR 2026 paper this codebase accompanies, and the concepts it defines (method, experiments, datasets, training objectives), each linked to the scripts that implement it.

tour.title: Project Overview and Pipeline
tour.description: README.txt is the run guide and the closest thing this project has to an entry point. It describes one three-stage pipeline used for every experiment: train a GPT, train VQ-VAEs on the GPT's hidden states, then compute mutual information (MI) between the learned discrete codes. The same pipeline runs on four task families (CFG, short and long path finding, and OpenWebText), each with a next-token (NTP) and a multi-token (MTP/'mtl') variant. Keep this train, quantize, measure loop in mind for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: The Paper Behind the Code
tour.description: This repository is the code release for 'Internal Planning in Language Models: Characterizing Horizon and Branch Awareness' (ICLR 2026). The paper asks how far ahead decoder-only LMs plan and whether they keep alternative continuations in mind. Its method compresses hidden states into VQ-VAE codes and measures mutual information between them. Three experiments use it: planning horizon (§3.1, the mi_calc_minimal / path_finding_mi_calc scripts), branch awareness (§3.2, mi_calc_full_path*), and information across layers and blocks (§3.3, the NLP_* scripts). Each concept node here links to the files that implement it.

tour.title: Synthetic CFG Datasets
tour.description: The first task family is a synthetic hierarchical context-free grammar. CFG_data_generation.py defines the grammar class, which samples random production rules, generates sequences in parallel and checks them with a fast parser. The full-sequence and prefix scripts load a pickled grammar instance and write padded binary corpora with BOS tokens. Because the grammar is known exactly, later steps can check whether model completions are valid.
tour.languageLesson: Python's pickle module serializes whole objects, so the generated grammar, with its rules and methods, can be saved once and reloaded by the other scripts. This keeps every dataset split consistent with the same grammar.

tour.title: Path-Finding Graph Datasets
tour.description: The second task family is path finding on random tree-like graphs that contain correct paths and decoy paths. path_finding_generate_multi_cpu.py splits generation across worker processes that write temporary JSONL files, then merges them into the final splits. Each split (train, val, vqvae, mi, and so on) has its own JSON config. For example, the PF_15XL train config produces 16M samples with up to 28 nodes, 2 paths and 2 decoys. This generator has one of the highest fan-ins in the graph, because many configs and downstream scripts depend on it.
tour.languageLesson: JSONL (JSON Lines) stores one JSON record per line. Parallel workers can each write their own file and the results can be merged by simple concatenation. A reader can also stream the records one at a time instead of loading the whole dataset.

tour.title: OpenWebText Natural Language
tour.description: The third task family uses real text. prepare.py downloads OpenWebText through HuggingFace datasets, tokenizes it in parallel with the GPT-2 BPE tokenizer from tiktoken, and writes train.bin and val.bin as flat uint16 token arrays. The readme next to it records the output size: about 9B training tokens. Compared with the synthetic CFG and path tasks from Steps 2-3, this tests whether the analysis still holds on natural language.
tour.languageLesson: numpy.memmap maps a binary file on disk straight into an array, so training scripts can take random slices of a multi-gigabyte token file without loading all of it into RAM. uint16 is enough here because GPT-2's vocabulary (50257) is smaller than 65536.

tour.title: Transformer Building Blocks
tour.description: With the datasets covered, the tour moves to the model library. modules.py provides the basic pieces: LayerNorm, rotary positional embeddings, rotary self-attention with flash-attention support, an MLP and a TransformerBlock. These blocks are reused by the VQ-VAE encoders and decoders later on, so the same attention mechanism appears both in the GPT and in the models that compress the GPT's hidden states.
tour.languageLesson: Rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) encode position by rotating query and key vectors by a position-dependent angle. Attention scores then depend on the relative distance between tokens, and no learned position table is needed.

tour.title: The GPT Model
tour.description: model.py is the GPT that every experiment trains. Along with the usual rotary-attention transformer, it has multi-token-prediction (mtl) heads and losses, generation with EOS handling, and APIs for extracting hidden states. That last feature connects the stages: the VQ-VAE and MI scripts call into a trained GPT to read its internal representations. model.py and minimal_VQVAEs.py have the highest fan-in in the project.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-token prediction adds extra output heads that predict tokens t+2, t+3, ... in addition to t+1. With 'shared heads', most parameters are reused across offsets. The extra loss terms push the hidden state to encode information about the future, which is the effect this project measures.

tour.title: Training GPTs on CFG
tour.description: llm_train.py is the first runnable script in the README workflow. It trains the GPT from Step 6 on the CFG data from Step 2, using next-token or multi-token targets, with DDP support and periodic accuracy checks. llm_train_utils.py supplies the cosine LR schedule with warmup, metadata export, and a parallel check of whether model completions are valid under the grammar. Each experiment directory holds a Python config. The mtl4 variant shown here enables shared-head MTL with mtl_length=4 on the same dataset as the NTP baseline.
tour.languageLesson: These nanoGPT-style configs are plain Python files whose top-level variables are executed into the training script's globals, overriding the defaults. That is why switching from NTP to MTP only requires pointing at a different config file.

tour.title: Path-Finding and NLP Training
tour.description: The same GPT is trained on the other two task families. path_finding_llm_train.py uses PathFindingDataset from path_finding_llm_utilities.py, which builds a vocabulary from the JSONL graphs of Step 3, tokenizes edges and paths, and can mask the loss on edge tokens. It also reports path accuracy. NLP_llm_train.py trains on the memmapped OpenWebText bins from Step 4 with mixed precision and gradient accumulation, configured by configGPT3Xsmall.py (an 8-layer, 512-dim GPT).
tour.languageLesson: PyTorch's DistributedSampler gives each DDP process a disjoint shard of the Dataset. That is why the path-finding script uses a DataLoader-based dataset, while the OpenWebText script samples random windows directly from a memmap.

tour.title: VQ-VAE Model Library
tour.description: The second stage compresses GPT hidden states into discrete codes. minimal_VQVAEs.py defines many VQ-VAE variants (single, two-stage, layer/block, last-token, path, 3v2, 61) with encoders and decoders built from the modules.py blocks of Step 5. It also tracks codebook usage and includes cosine-push and soft-entropy regularizers. vqvae_utils.py is the shared helper library: optimizer, LR and beta schedules, masked NRMSE reconstruction metrics, and a wrapper that loads a trained GPT checkpoint and extracts its hidden states.
tour.languageLesson: A VQ-VAE replaces each continuous encoder output with the nearest vector in a learned codebook. Gradients pass through the non-differentiable lookup with the straight-through estimator, and a commitment loss weighted by beta keeps encoder outputs close to their chosen codes.

tour.title: Training VQ-VAEs on CFG
tour.description: These scripts apply the VQ-VAE library to a frozen CFG GPT from Step 7. train_minimal_vqvae1.py trains the first-stage, layer-wise VQVAE1. train_minimal_vqvae2.py then loads that frozen VQVAE1 and trains VQVAE2 on its normalized outputs, forming a two-stage hierarchy. train_minimal_vqvae_single.py trains a single-representation baseline. Each run is configured by a JSON file in the experiment folder that sets codebook size, iteration count and output directory.

tour.title: Path and NLP VQ-VAE Variants
tour.description: The other tasks need VQ-VAEs tailored to their structure. On path finding, path_finding_vqvae61_train.py trains VQVAE61, which encodes hidden representations across several time steps for the long task. path_vqvae_train.py learns codes directly over the path token sequences, giving the target variable that MI is measured against. For OpenWebText, NLP_vqvae_layer_and_block_train.py quantizes hidden states per layer or per block of layers, and the matching layer_and_block config sets T=256.

tour.title: Information-Theory Toolkit
tour.description: Before the final stage, the tour covers the math it uses. information_theory_utils.py provides StreamingInfo, a count table that can be filled incrementally from streamed batches. It estimates entropy, joint and conditional entropy, mutual information and conditional MI over the discrete VQ-VAE codes. It offers both plug-in estimates and bias-corrected Paninski/BUB estimates, which matters because large codebooks make plug-in MI estimates biased upward.
tour.languageLesson: Mutual information I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y) measures how much knowing one code reduces uncertainty about another. With finite samples and many possible symbol pairs, the plug-in estimate overstates I, so bias corrections such as BUB are needed for reliable comparisons.

tour.title: Computing Mutual Information
tour.description: The MI scripts bring all three stages together. For each task, they run a trained GPT (Steps 6-8), quantize its hidden states with trained VQ-VAEs (Steps 9-11), and stream the resulting codes into StreamingInfo (Step 12). mi_calc_minimal.py does this for CFG, mi_calc_full_path.py compares GPT-state codes with Path_VQVAE codes across a full generated path, and NLP_mi_calc_v6 2.py measures MI between per-block and last-token codes on OpenWebText. Comparing these MI values between NTP and MTP models is the project's central experiment.
